Why is RAM so expensive right now? I priced a real white build on PCPartPicker (US prices, 15 September 2026). 16GB of DDR5, the TEAMGROUP T-Force Vulcan 2x8GB DDR5-6000 CL38, came to $239.99. That is more than the motherboard ($139.99), the CPU ($163.00) and the case ($159.90). The reason: Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron shifted production capacity to HBM memory for AI data centres, which pays them better than consumer DDR5. On 5 September 2026 the 32GB memory tier was indexed at $15.31-20.31 per GB, and analysts do not expect relief before late 2027. I can't make RAM cheaper. A GPU that doesn't fit is money you can't use until you return it. So check dimensions before you buy.

For this build I pulled the GPU size straight from asus.com: the ASUS Dual Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB White is 202 x 120 x 49 mm. The case, a Thermalright TR-A70 Vision White, is 450.8 x 289.5 x 477 mm with glass on the front, side and top.

One warning: a case's outside size isn't its GPU clearance. Look up the case's max GPU length as well, and leave room for fans and cables.

You can order white fans for the lighting and get fans with no lighting at all. The difference is one letter.

Thermalright TL-C12CW-S (with the -S) is ARGB. The plain TL-C12CW has no lighting. Same brand, same white, one letter apart in the part number.

In my white build I used the plain TL-C12CW on purpose: 2 at the rear as exhaust, $8.39 each. The lit fans are 3 Montech GF120 V2 ARGB at the bottom as intake. The commenter asked for RGB but not everywhere, so the plain ones were the right call here. If you want them lit, you need the -S.

Read the full part number before you check out. Prices: PCPartPicker, US, 15 September 2026.

Not enough ARGB headers on your motherboard? Count before you buy, not after.

The board in this build, an ASRock B850M Pro RS WiFi White, has three ARGB headers. All three are used:
- the case strip
- the cooler
- the fan hub

The lit fans share one header through the hub. Without it, there'd be nowhere left to plug them in.

Count your lit parts against your board's headers before you order.
